questions.prompt: Typical human somatic cells are _____, with two sets of chromosomes.
questions.hint: They carry maternal and paternal sets.
questions.explanation: Diploidy describes chromosome-set number, not whether a chromosome has replicated.

questions.prompt: The human haploid chromosome number is _____.
questions.hint: A sperm or ovum carries one set.
questions.explanation: Human gametes contain 22 autosomes plus one sex chromosome.

questions.prompt: A maternal and paternal chromosome with corresponding gene loci form a _____ pair.
questions.hint: The pair can have different alleles.
questions.explanation: Homologous chromosomes pair during meiosis I and separate in anaphase I.

questions.prompt: The duplicated copies of one chromosome are called _____ chromatids.
questions.hint: These are products of DNA replication.
questions.explanation: Sister chromatids are held together until separation in mitosis or meiosis II.

questions.prompt: The position of a gene along a chromosome is its _____.
questions.explanation: A locus refers to location; an allele refers to a variant at that location.

questions.prompt: In meiosis I, _____ chromosomes separate.
questions.explanation: The separation makes cells haploid even while chromosomes still have sister chromatids.

questions.prompt: In meiosis II, sister _____ separate.
questions.hint: This is not a second homologue separation.
questions.explanation: Meiosis II separates chromosome copies after the first reductional division.

questions.prompt: Crossing over typically occurs during prophase _____.
questions.explanation: Paired homologues exchange DNA during prophase I.

questions.prompt: A paired set of two replicated homologues contains _____ chromatids.
questions.explanation: A tetrad includes four chromatids, not four separate homologous chromosomes.

questions.prompt: Random orientation of homologous pairs occurs at metaphase _____.
questions.explanation: Metaphase I orientation varies among chromosomes and cells.

questions.prompt: Hydra budding is an example of _____ reproduction.
questions.hint: A single individual produces an offspring.
questions.explanation: Budding does not require sperm–egg fusion.

questions.prompt: Genetically very similar descendants of one source are termed _____.
questions.explanation: Clones can differ genetically through subsequent changes despite common origin.

questions.prompt: Fusion of two gametes is called _____.
questions.explanation: Fertilization restores the combined parental chromosome sets.

questions.prompt: The cell formed after gametes unite is the _____.
questions.hint: The earliest stage of a new animal individual.
questions.explanation: A zygote normally contains one haploid chromosome set from each parent.

questions.prompt: The original source of new alleles is _____.
questions.hint: Distinguish new DNA variants from chromosome shuffling.
questions.explanation: Mutation changes genetic sequence; assortment and recombination rearrange variants already present.

questions.prompt: Mendel's first law says alleles _____ during gamete formation.
questions.hint: Only one allele usually reaches each gamete.
questions.explanation: The two alleles separate when homologous chromosome copies segregate.

questions.prompt: The allelic makeup of an individual is its _____.
questions.explanation: Genotype describes inherited genetic composition, not necessarily visible traits.

questions.prompt: An organism's observable trait is its _____.
questions.explanation: Phenotype results from genotype interacting with development and environment.

questions.prompt: An Aa individual is _____ at that locus.
questions.explanation: Heterozygotes carry two different alleles for the gene.

questions.prompt: An AA individual is _____ at that locus.
questions.hint: The two alleles are the same.
questions.explanation: Homozygotes carry two copies of the same allele.

questions.prompt: Aa × Aa produces an expected genotype ratio of _____.
questions.hint: List AA, Aa, and aa in that order.
questions.explanation: One AA, two heterozygote combinations, and one aa are expected.

questions.prompt: Under complete dominance, an Aa × Aa cross has a _____ dominant-to-recessive phenotype ratio.
questions.hint: Three of four possible offspring show dominance.
questions.explanation: The predicted fraction is 3/4 dominant and 1/4 recessive.

questions.prompt: To test whether A_ is AA or Aa, cross it with _____.
questions.hint: The tester's recessive genotype is known.
questions.explanation: A recessive tester makes the unknown parent's a allele visible in offspring if present.

questions.prompt: A predicted 25% offspring probability does not _____ an exact fraction in a small family.
questions.explanation: Probabilities describe long-run expectations, not deterministic offspring orders.

questions.prompt: For independent events, the _____ rule multiplies their probabilities.
questions.hint: Used when both outcomes must happen.
questions.explanation: Independent 1/2 chances both occurring yield 1/4.

questions.prompt: A standard AaBb × AaBb cross gives a _____ phenotype ratio when genes assort independently.
questions.hint: Requires complete dominance and unlinked inheritance.
questions.explanation: Nine, three, three, and one describe four phenotype classes.

questions.prompt: Genes close together on the same chromosome are genetically _____.
questions.explanation: Physical linkage can reduce independent assortment.

questions.prompt: The A and B alleles of the ABO blood group show _____.
questions.hint: Neither A nor B disappears in an AB individual.
questions.explanation: Both antigen phenotypes are expressed in IᴬIᴮ people.

questions.prompt: When one gene affects several phenotypes, this is _____.
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy is different from polygenic inheritance.

questions.prompt: A single trait affected by many genes is a _____ trait.
questions.explanation: Complex traits need not follow one-gene Mendelian ratios.

questions.prompt: Inbreeding tends to increase genetic _____ at loci.
questions.hint: The same allele may arrive from both parents.
questions.explanation: More homozygous recessive combinations can expose deleterious variants.

questions.prompt: The radish–cabbage hybrid shown in the lecture is called _____.
questions.hint: A botanical example of rapid hybrid speciation.
questions.explanation: The original hybrid was sterile until chromosome doubling enabled more regular meiosis.

questions.prompt: Genome doubling after hybridization between species can produce _____.
questions.hint: Multiple chromosome sets from different species.
questions.explanation: Allopolyploidy is especially important in plant evolutionary history.

questions.prompt: Most classic autosomal recessive disorders require _____ pathogenic alleles at the locus.
questions.hint: One from each parent in a typical diploid individual.
questions.explanation: A single carrier may be unaffected under classic recessive inheritance.

questions.prompt: The sterile Raphanobrassica hybrid regained fertility through chromosome _____.
questions.explanation: Genome doubling can stabilize meiotic pairing in interspecies hybrids.

questions.prompt: Mendelian genes occupy specific positions on chromosomes called _____.
questions.explanation: A locus is a physical location on a chromosome.

questions.prompt: _____ used fruit flies to provide evidence for the chromosome theory of inheritance.
questions.explanation: Morgan's crosses connected sex-linked eye color with the X chromosome.

questions.prompt: The genus of the model fruit fly used by Morgan is _____.
questions.hint: Small flies with rapid breeding cycles.
questions.explanation: Drosophila melanogaster is a foundational organism in genetics.

questions.prompt: The common reference phenotype in a population is called _____.
questions.explanation: Wild type denotes the standard observed form, not a genotype lacking mutations.

questions.prompt: Morgan's classic alternative to red fruit-fly eyes was a _____ eye phenotype.
questions.explanation: The white-eye allele is X-linked in the classic fruit-fly example.

questions.prompt: A gene found on the X chromosome is _____-linked.
questions.explanation: X linkage yields characteristic patterns in XY and XX organisms.

questions.prompt: A gene found on the Y chromosome is _____-linked.
questions.explanation: Y-linked loci can track paternal Y-chromosome ancestry.

questions.prompt: Genes in mitochondria and chloroplasts are _____ genes.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and plant plastids contain DNA separate from nuclear chromosomes.

questions.prompt: Human mitochondrial DNA is typically inherited from the _____.
questions.explanation: The egg normally supplies the mitochondria retained after fertilization.

questions.prompt: An individual containing cells from distinct zygotic origins can exhibit genetic _____.
questions.explanation: The instructor's visual example is not accompanied by a specific case explanation.

questions.prompt: The isotope _____ was used to mark phage DNA in the Hershey–Chase experiment.
questions.explanation: ³²P was associated mainly with bacteria following infection and separation.

questions.prompt: Phage protein coats were marked using _____.
questions.explanation: ³⁵S was found mainly outside infected cells after blending.

questions.prompt: A virus that infects bacteria is a _____.
questions.explanation: Bacteriophages inject genetic material into bacterial host cells.

questions.prompt: Following centrifugation, bacterial cells collected in the _____.
questions.explanation: The bacterial pellet retained most DNA-specific radiolabel.

questions.prompt: Most detached phage protein coats remained in the _____ above the pellet.
questions.explanation: The liquid contained the protein-specific sulfur label.

questions.prompt: Adenine and guanine are the two DNA _____.
questions.explanation: A and G are purines; C and T are pyrimidines.

questions.prompt: Cytosine and thymine are DNA _____.
questions.explanation: In RNA, uracil replaces thymine in ordinary canonical bases.

questions.prompt: In DNA, adenine pairs with _____.
questions.explanation: A pairs with T; G pairs with C.

questions.prompt: RNA contains the sugar _____.
questions.explanation: The 2′-hydroxyl of ribose distinguishes RNA from DNA sugar.

questions.prompt: The copying of DNA before cell division is DNA _____.
questions.explanation: Replication conserves genetic sequence through complementary base pairing.

questions.prompt: The synthesis of RNA from a DNA template is _____.
questions.hint: Occurs in the nucleus for most eukaryotic nuclear genes.
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase makes RNA complementary to a DNA template.

questions.prompt: Ribosome-guided assembly of amino acids from an mRNA message is _____.
questions.hint: Second step for protein-coding gene expression.
questions.explanation: Translation follows codon instructions to produce a polypeptide.

questions.prompt: A coding triplet of mRNA bases is called a _____.
questions.explanation: Standard codons encode an amino acid or signal translation to stop.

questions.prompt: The RNA intermediate read by ribosomes is _____ RNA.
questions.explanation: mRNA is translated into polypeptide sequence at ribosomes.

questions.prompt: Protein synthesis by translation occurs on a _____.
questions.hint: A molecular machine, not the nucleus.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes coordinate decoding and peptide-bond formation.

questions.prompt: Darwin's term for inheritance with changes across generations was descent with _____.
questions.hint: The phrase names an evolutionary process.
questions.explanation: Variation accumulates along branching lineages descended from ancestors.

questions.prompt: A branching diagram of evolutionary relationships is a _____ tree.
questions.explanation: Phylogenies represent hypotheses about lineage splitting and common ancestry.

questions.prompt: The author associated with binomial nomenclature is Carl _____.
questions.explanation: Linnaeus standardized the genus-plus-species format.

questions.prompt: Darwin published On the Origin of Species in _____.
questions.explanation: The book established an influential scientific case for evolution by natural selection.

questions.prompt: The scientist nicknamed Darwin's Bulldog was Thomas Henry _____.
questions.hint: Advocate rather than co-originator of selection.
questions.explanation: Huxley strongly defended evolutionary theory in public debate.

questions.prompt: Random allele-frequency change caused by chance sampling is genetic _____.
questions.explanation: Drift is distinct from geographic vicariance, though they may interact.

questions.prompt: Geographic separation by a newly formed barrier is _____.
questions.hint: For example, a barrier separating a population.
questions.explanation: Vicariance is range splitting, not a synonym for random drift.

questions.prompt: Selection based on differences in mating success is _____ selection.
questions.hint: Examples include mate choice and contests.
questions.explanation: Sexual selection can favor structures or behavior enhancing reproductive success.

questions.prompt: The fraction of gene copies representing a variant in a population is its allele _____.
questions.explanation: Allele-frequency change is a core population-genetic description of evolution.

questions.prompt: When inherited traits produce different reproductive success, _____ selection can occur.
questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on heritable variation through differential reproductive contribution.

questions.prompt: A reproductive barrier preventing fertilization is called _____.
questions.explanation: Habitat, timing, behavior or gamete incompatibility can prevent a zygote.

questions.prompt: A barrier causing hybrid sterility after fertilization is _____.
questions.explanation: Postzygotic barriers can impair hybrid viability or fertility.

questions.prompt: The evolutionary origin of a distinct species is _____.
questions.explanation: Reproductive isolation is one important route to divergence.

questions.prompt: The disappearance of many species in a geologically short interval is a mass _____.
questions.explanation: Mass extinctions can restructure ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.prompt: Rapid diversification into ecological opportunities is adaptive _____.
questions.explanation: Adaptive radiation can produce many descendant species.
